records.source: ה֣וֹי רֹעִ֗ים מְאַבְּדִ֧ים וּמְפִצִ֛ים אֶת־צֹ֥אן מַרְעִיתִ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Woe [to] shepherds destroying and scattering [the] flock of my pasture, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Woe to the shepherds who are destroying and scattering the sheep of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} pasture, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.1: Woe, shepherds who destroy and scatter the flock of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} pasture, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.1: How terrible it will be for the shepherds who are destroying {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and scattering the sheep I feed in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own pasture, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: shepherds: the kings and rulers of Judah
decisions.reason: Kings in the ancient Near East were called the shepherds of their people, and Jeremiah uses the word for Judah's rulers (2:8; 10:21; 22:22). Coming straight after the oracles on the last kings of Judah in chapter 22, this woe is aimed at them.

decisions.choice: destroy: let the flock perish
decisions.reason: The verb means to destroy or to let perish. Said of sheep it can also mean letting them stray and be lost (50:6, "lost sheep"). Either way the rulers' neglect is ruining the flock.

decisions.choice: the flock of my pasture: the people belong to God, not to the shepherds
decisions.reason: God calls the people "my" flock, grazing in "my" pasture (Psalm 100:3; Ezekiel 34:31). The rulers only look after what is his, and he will call them to account for it (verse 2).

decisions.choice: Woe (Literal); Woe to (Balanced); How terrible it will be for (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for the cry of woe, as in Isaiah. Readable spells out the threat in plain words.

records.heading: Shepherds who scatter the flock

records.source: לָ֠כֵן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל עַֽל־הָרֹעִים֮ הָרֹעִ֣ים אֶת־עַמִּי֒ אַתֶּ֞ם הֲפִצֹתֶ֤ם אֶת־צֹאנִי֙ וַתַּדִּח֔וּם וְלֹ֥א פְקַדְתֶּ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם הִנְנִ֨י פֹקֵ֧ד עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם אֶת־רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel concerning the shepherds shepherding my people: you have scattered my flock and driven them away and not attended to them; look, I [am] attending to you [for the] evil of your deeds, declares Yahweh.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this about the shepherds who shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people: You have scattered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and chased them off, and you have not looked after them. So now I will look after you, and punish the evil you have done, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, concerning the shepherds who shepherd {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people: You have scattered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and driven them away, and you have not attended to them; look, I am about to attend to you [for] the evil of your deeds, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says to the shepherds who take care of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people: You have scattered {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock and chased them away. You did not take care of them. So now I will take care of you: I will punish you for the evil things you have done, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: attend to: the same verb for caring for the flock and for punishing its shepherds
decisions.reason: The verb means to give attention to someone, either to care for them or to deal with them for what they have done. The shepherds have not given the flock attention, so God will give them attention, for their evil deeds. The play continues in verse 4, where none of the flock will be "missing" (the same verb again).

decisions.choice: scattered ... driven them away: what the shepherds' rule has led to
decisions.reason: The rulers' bad leadership is blamed for the scattering of the people. In verse 3 God says he himself drove them out: the exile is his judgment, and the rulers' failure brought it on.

decisions.choice: looked after ... look after (Balanced); take care of ... take care of (Readable), then "punish"
decisions.reason: The same English verb is used twice to keep the play on the Hebrew verb, and "punish" makes plain what the second "looking after" means.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); The LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for the formula at each level.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֗י אֲקַבֵּץ֙ אֶת־שְׁאֵרִ֣ית צֹאנִ֔י מִכֹּל֙ הָאֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־הִדַּ֥חְתִּי אֹתָ֖ם שָׁ֑ם וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֥י אֶתְהֶ֛ן עַל־נְוֵהֶ֖ן וּפָר֥וּ וְרָבֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And I will gather [the] remnant of my flock from all the lands where I have driven them there, and I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will be fruitful and multiply.
pieces: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will gather together the remnant of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from every country to which I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their grazing land, and they will be fruitful and increase.

L.3: And I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will gather the remnant of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from all the lands where I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their fold, and they will be fruitful and multiply.

R.3: Then I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will gather the rest of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flock from all the countries where I have scattered them. I will bring them back to their own pasture, and they will have many young and grow in number.

decisions.choice: I myself: God takes over the shepherds' work
decisions.reason: The word "I" is stressed. Where the rulers scattered the flock, God himself will gather it (31:10; Ezekiel 34:11-16). He also says that he is the one who drove them out: the exile came from him as judgment.

decisions.choice: remnant: those left after the judgment
decisions.reason: The word means what is left over. It is used for the people who survive war and exile (6:9; 24:8; Isaiah 10:20-22).

decisions.choice: be fruitful and multiply: the first blessing restored
decisions.reason: These are the words of God's blessing at creation and to Noah and Abraham's family (Genesis 1:28; 9:1; 35:11). Back in their land, the people will grow again as God first intended (3:16).

decisions.choice: pasture: the place where the flock lives and grazes
decisions.reason: The word means a grazing place or the home of a flock, and so also a dwelling (10:25; 33:12).

decisions.choice: have many young and grow in number
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of the flock instead of the older phrase "be fruitful and multiply".

records.source: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֧י עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם רֹעִ֖ים וְרָע֑וּם וְלֹא־יִֽירְא֨וּ ע֧וֹד וְלֹא־יֵחַ֛תּוּ וְלֹ֥א יִפָּקֵ֖דוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And I will raise up over them shepherds and they will shepherd them, and not they will fear again and not be dismayed and not be missing, declares Yahweh.
pieces: I will set shepherds over them who will truly tend them. They will no longer be afraid or terrified, and not one of them will be lost, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: And I will raise up shepherds over them, and they will shepherd them; and they will no longer fear or be dismayed, and none will be missing, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: I will give them shepherds who will take care of them. They will not be afraid or frightened anymore, and not one of them will be missing, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: shepherds: new rulers, given by God
decisions.reason: God promised "shepherds after my own heart" in 3:15. Here they come before the promise of one king from David's line (verse 5); the good king and the good leaders belong together.

decisions.choice: be missing: the third use of the verb in verses 2-4
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 2 ("attend to") here means to be looked for and not found, as when a flock is counted (1 Samuel 25:7). Under the new shepherds no sheep will be lost.

decisions.choice: truly tend them
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "truly" to bring out the contrast with the shepherds of verses 1-2, who did not look after the flock.

records.source: הִנֵּ֨ה יָמִ֤ים בָּאִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וַהֲקִמֹתִ֥י לְדָוִ֖ד צֶ֣מַח צַדִּ֑יק וּמָ֤לַךְ מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ וְהִשְׂכִּ֔יל וְעָשָׂ֛ה מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, and I will raise up for David a branch righteous, and he will reign [as] king and act wisely, and do justice and righteousness in the land.
pieces: The days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will raise a righteous Branch for David. \q He will reign as king and rule with wisdom, \q and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.

L.5: Look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, \q and he will reign as king and act wisely, \q and do justice and righteousness in the land.

R.5: The time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q when I will give David a righteous Branch, a king from his family. \q He will rule as king, and he will rule wisely. \q He will do what is just and righteous in the land.

decisions.choice: a righteous Branch for David: a coming king from David's line
decisions.reason: A branch is new growth that springs from a plant. God promises a king who will come from the family of David, though the kings of chapter 22 have failed and Coniah's line is cut off (22:30). Jeremiah repeats this promise in 33:15, and later prophets use "Branch" as a title for the coming king (Zechariah 3:8; 6:12; compare Isaiah 4:2; 11:1). The New Testament sees God's promise to David fulfilled in Jesus (Luke 1:32-33).

decisions.choice: righteous: a king who is himself in the right and rules rightly
decisions.reason: The word can mean a rightful or legitimate heir, and it also means one who does what is right. Both fit: the king will be the true heir of David, and he will do what the last kings did not (22:3, 13-17).

decisions.choice: act wisely: rule with good sense, and so succeed
decisions.reason: The verb means to act with insight, and so also to prosper (Joshua 1:7-8; 1 Samuel 18:14). A wise ruler is a successful one. The other king named in 22:30 will "not prosper" (a different verb).

decisions.choice: do justice and righteousness: what God asks of a king
decisions.reason: God told the kings of Judah to do justice and righteousness (22:3), and praised Josiah for doing it (22:15). David himself did so (2 Samuel 8:15). The promised king will do what his fathers were called to do.

decisions.choice: Branch, with a capital letter
decisions.reason: The capital letter marks the word as a title for the king, as in 33:15. Isaiah 4:2 uses the same Hebrew word in a passage where it may mean the land's new crops, and there it stays lowercase.

decisions.choice: a king from his family
decisions.reason: Readable says who the Branch is, from the rest of the verse.

records.heading: A Branch for David

records.source: בְּיָמָיו֙ תִּוָּשַׁ֣ע יְהוּדָ֔ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִשְׁכֹּ֣ן לָבֶ֑טַח וְזֶה־שְּׁמ֥וֹ אֲֽשֶׁר־יִקְרְא֖וֹ יְהוָ֥ה׀צִדְקֵֽנוּ׃ס
records.gloss: In his days will be saved Judah and Israel will dwell in security; and this [is] his name which he will call him: Yahweh [is] our righteousness.
pieces: In his days Judah will be saved, \q and Israel will live in safety. \q And this is the name people will give him: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Is Our Righteousness."

L.6: In his days Judah will be saved, \q and Israel will dwell in security; \q and this [is] his name that one will call him: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] our righteousness."

R.6: While he is king, Judah will be saved, \q and Israel will live in safety. \q People will call him by this name: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} Is Our Righteousness."

decisions.choice: The LORD is our righteousness: a name that says what God will do for his people
decisions.reason: The name is a sentence: the LORD is the one who gives his people what is right and puts them in the right. Righteousness here is more than a quality of God; it is his saving justice, which sets his people free and makes things right (Isaiah 45:24-25; 46:13). The same name is given to Jerusalem in 33:16.

decisions.choice: a play on the name of King Zedekiah
decisions.reason: The last king of Judah, Zedekiah, was set on the throne by Babylon (2 Kings 24:17). His name means "the LORD is my righteousness" or "the LORD is righteous". The name of the promised king turns the same two words around: what Zedekiah's name claimed and his reign never showed, the coming king will truly be. The text does not name Zedekiah here, but the likeness of the two names is close and hard to miss.

decisions.choice: that one will call him: people in general will call him
alternatives: which the LORD will call him
decisions.reason: The verb is "he will call him" with no subject named, the Hebrew way of saying "he will be called". The Septuagint seems to have read the subject as the LORD and gives a different name, close to "Josedek" (this is from general knowledge). The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: Judah and Israel: the whole people, south and north, together again
decisions.reason: Israel, the northern kingdom, had been taken into exile long before (2 Kings 17). Jeremiah promises that both parts of the nation will be restored together (3:18; 31:27, 31).

decisions.choice: The LORD Is Our Righteousness, written as a name
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set the words out as a proper name with capitals; Literal shows the bare Hebrew with the verb supplied. The same wording is used in 33:16.

decisions.choice: While he is king
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in his days" means: during his reign.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן הִנֵּֽה־יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹא־יֹ֤אמְרוּ עוֹד֙ חַי־יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֶעֱלָ֛ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Therefore look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, and not they will say again, [By the] life of Yahweh who brought up [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt,
pieces: Therefore, the days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when it will no longer be said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who brought up the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} from the land of Egypt,"

L.7: Therefore, look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when they will no longer say, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who brought up the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from the land of Egypt,"

R.7: So a time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when people will no longer make a promise by saying, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, the God who led the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of Egypt."

decisions.choice: verses 7-8 repeat 16:14-15
decisions.reason: These two verses say almost word for word what 16:14-15 says, and the wording at every level is kept the same wherever the Hebrew is the same. There the promise follows a word of judgment; here it follows the promise of the king and the gathering of the flock (verses 3-6). In this verse the one difference is "they will say" where 16:14 has "it will be said"; verse 8 notes the rest.

decisions.choice: As the LORD lives: the form of a solemn oath
decisions.reason: An Israelite swore by the life of the LORD (4:2; 5:2; 12:16). The words that follow name him by his greatest act until now: bringing Israel out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: a new exodus that will outshine the first
decisions.reason: The return from exile will be so great that people will name God by it instead of by the exodus from Egypt (16:14-15; Isaiah 43:16-19).

decisions.choice: [As] the LORD lives (L); As surely as the LORD lives (B, R); Readable adds "make a promise by saying" and "the God who led"
decisions.reason: The same wording as 16:14, so that the repeated verses read alike. Balanced also gives "they will no longer say" as 16:14 gives its Hebrew, "it will no longer be said"; the impersonal sense is the same.

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־חַי־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶעֱלָה֩ וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵבִ֜יא אֶת־זֶ֨רַע בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹנָה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָֽאֲרָצ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִדַּחְתִּ֖ים שָׁ֑ם וְיָשְׁב֖וּ עַל־אַדְמָתָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: but rather [by the] life of Yahweh who brought up and who brought [the] offspring of [the] house of Israel from [the] land of [the] north and from all the lands where I had driven them there; and they will dwell on their land.
pieces: but, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who brought up and led the descendants of the house of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where I had driven them." Then they will live in their own land.

L.8: but, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, who brought up and who led the offspring of the house of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where I had driven them." And they will dwell on their own land.

R.8: Instead they will say, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, the God who led the descendants of Israel out of the land in the north and out of all the countries where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had scattered them." Then they will live in their own land.

decisions.choice: differences from 16:15
decisions.reason: Where 16:15 has one verb, "brought up", this verse has two, "brought up and led"; where 16:15 has "the {children} of Israel", this verse has "the offspring of the house of Israel"; where 16:15 has "he had driven them", this verse has "I had driven them"; and where 16:15 ends "I will bring them back to their land that I gave to their fathers", this verse ends "they will dwell on their own land".

decisions.choice: where I had driven them: God's own voice breaks into the oath
decisions.reason: Inside the words people will say, the Hebrew has "I had driven them", as if God himself finished the sentence; 16:15 has "he" here. The meaning is the same: God both sent them away and brings them back.

decisions.choice: the land of the north: Babylon, the land of exile
decisions.reason: Invaders came on Judah from the north (1:14; 4:6; 6:22), since the road from Babylon ran round by the north, and the exiles were taken away by the same road.

decisions.choice: where he had scattered them
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the speakers' own voice in the oath, as 16:15 has it, so that the reader is not confused by a sudden "I" in the people's words. Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's "I". "Scattered" is Readable's plainer word for "driven", as in 16:15.

decisions.choice: Instead they will say; the God who led
decisions.reason: As in 16:15: Readable ends verse 7 with a full sentence, so it repeats the verb here, and it says "the God who led" so that the oath clearly names the LORD by what he did.

records.source: לַנְּבִאִ֞ים נִשְׁבַּ֧ר לִבִּ֣י בְקִרְבִּ֗י רָֽחֲפוּ֙ כָּל־עַצְמוֹתַ֔י הָיִ֨יתִי֙ כְּאִ֣ישׁ שִׁכּ֔וֹרוּכְגֶ֖בֶר עֲבָ֣רוֹ יָ֑יִן מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וּמִפְּנֵ֖י דִּבְרֵ֥י קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: Concerning the prophets: is broken my heart in my midst, tremble all my bones; I have become like a man drunk and like a man [whom] has passed over him wine, because of Yahweh and because of [the] words of his holiness.
pieces: Concerning the prophets: \q My heart is crushed inside me, and all my bones are shaking. \q I am like a drunk man, \q like someone overpowered by wine, \q because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy words.

L.9: Concerning the prophets: \q My heart is broken inside me; all my bones shake; \q I have become like a drunken man, \q like a man whom wine has overcome, \q because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy words.

R.9: About the prophets: \q My heart is broken, and my whole body shakes. \q I am like a man who is drunk, \q who has had too much wine, \q because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy words.

decisions.choice: Concerning the prophets: the title of verses 9-40
decisions.reason: The words stand as a heading for the long collection that follows, as "To the house of the king of Judah" heads 21:11-22:30 and as the names of nations head the oracles of chapters 46-49.

decisions.choice: my heart, my bones: Jeremiah speaks
decisions.reason: The speaker names the LORD as "the LORD" and is shaken by his words, so these are the prophet's own words, as in 4:19 and 8:18. From verse 11 God speaks.

decisions.choice: shake: go weak and tremble
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. Elsewhere it is used of a bird hovering over its young (Deuteronomy 32:11) and of the Spirit over the waters (Genesis 1:2). Here it seems to mean that the prophet's body trembles and loses its strength.

decisions.choice: like a drunken man: overwhelmed and unsteady
decisions.reason: The prophet is not drunk; he staggers like a drunk man because God's holy words have overcome him. What he must say about the prophets has shaken him to the core.

decisions.choice: my whole body shakes
decisions.reason: Readable says "my whole body" for "all my bones", the Hebrew way of speaking of the whole person.

records.heading: Concerning the prophets

records.source: כִּ֤י מְנָֽאֲפִים֙ מָלְאָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּֽי־מִפְּנֵ֤י אָלָה֙ אָבְלָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ יָבְשׁ֖וּ נְא֣וֹת מִדְבָּ֑ר וַתְּהִ֤י מְרֽוּצָתָם֙ רָעָ֔ה וּגְבוּרָתָ֖ם לֹא־כֵֽן׃
records.gloss: For [with] adulterers is full the land; for because of a curse mourns the land, are dried up [the] pastures of [the] wilderness; and is their course evil, and their might [is] not right.
pieces: The land is full of adulterers. \q The land mourns under the curse, \q and the wilderness pastures have withered. \q They run their race toward evil, \q and they use their power for what is wrong.

L.10: For the land is full of adulterers; \q for because of a curse the land mourns; \q the pastures of the wilderness have dried up. \q And their course has become evil, \q and their strength [is] not right.

R.10: The land is full of people who are unfaithful in marriage. \q Because of the curse, the land is dry and dying, \q and the grass in the open country has dried up. \q The people rush to do evil, \q and they use their power in the wrong way.

decisions.choice: adulterers: unfaithful to their marriages and to God
decisions.reason: Jeremiah charges the people with adultery in the plain sense (5:7-8; 7:9; 29:23), and he also calls their worship of other gods adultery (3:8-9). Verse 14 says the prophets themselves do it.

decisions.choice: a curse: the curse of the covenant
decisions.reason: The covenant warned that if the people broke it, the sky would hold back rain and the land would fail (11:3-8; Deuteronomy 28:15, 23-24). The drought is the curse coming true (14:1-6).

decisions.choice: mourns: dries up and withers
decisions.reason: The verb means to mourn, and when used of the land, to dry up (12:4; Amos 1:2). Both pictures are here: the land grieves, and the land withers.

decisions.choice: their course ... their strength: the way they live and the power they use
decisions.reason: "Course" is the running of a race (8:6). "Their" may mean the people of the land or the prophets and priests of verse 11; they run hard after evil and use their strength for wrong.

decisions.choice: dry and dying
decisions.reason: Readable puts the two senses of the verb (m3) into plain words.

records.source: כִּֽי־גַם־נָבִ֥יא גַם־כֹּהֵ֖ן חָנֵ֑פוּ גַּם־בְּבֵיתִ֛י מָצָ֥אתִי רָעָתָ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: For both prophet and priest are polluted; even in my house I have found their evil, declares Yahweh.
pieces: For both prophet and priest are godless; \q even in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own house I have found their wickedness, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.11: For both prophet and priest are polluted; \q even in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house I have found their evil, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.11: Both the prophets and the priests have turned away from God. \q I have found them doing evil even in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own house, the temple, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: polluted: godless, unclean before God
decisions.reason: The verb is used of land made unclean by bloodshed and sin (3:1-2, 9; Numbers 35:33), and of people who have turned from God (Isaiah 24:5). The leaders of worship have become profane.

decisions.choice: my house: the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: God calls the temple his house. Wrong was done even there: idols and false worship (7:10-11, 30; 32:34).

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my house" means.

records.source: לָכֵן֩ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה דַרְכָּ֜ם לָהֶ֗ם כַּחֲלַקְלַקּוֹת֙ בָּֽאֲפֵלָ֔ה יִדַּ֖חוּ וְנָ֣פְלוּ בָ֑הּ כִּֽי־אָבִ֨יא עֲלֵיהֶ֥ם רָעָ֛ה שְׁנַ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Therefore will be their way to them like slippery places in the darkness; they will be pushed and fall in it; for I will bring on them disaster, [the] year of their punishment, declares Yahweh.
pieces: So their path will become like slippery ground in the dark; \q they will be pushed down, and there they will fall. \q For I will bring disaster on them in the year I punish them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: Therefore their way will be to them like slippery places in the darkness; \q they will be thrust down and fall in it; \q for I will bring disaster on them, the year of their punishment, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: So the road they walk on will be slippery and dark. \q They will be pushed, and they will fall. \q I will bring disaster on them when it is time for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to punish them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: slippery places in the darkness: a path where no one can keep their footing
decisions.reason: A psalm prays that the way of the wicked may be "dark and slippery" (Psalm 35:6). Walking in the dark on a slippery path, they cannot see where they go or keep from falling (13:16).

decisions.choice: the year of their punishment: the time God deals with them
decisions.reason: The word for punishment comes from the verb of verse 2, "attend to": it is the time when God visits them to settle accounts (11:23; 48:44).

records.source: וּבִנְבִיאֵ֥י שֹׁמְר֖וֹן רָאִ֣יתִי תִפְלָ֑ה הִנַּבְּא֣וּ בַבַּ֔עַל וַיַּתְע֥וּ אֶת־עַמִּ֖י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And among [the] prophets of Samaria I saw an offensive thing: they prophesied by Baal and led astray my people Israel.
pieces: Among the prophets of Samaria I saw something repulsive: \q they prophesied by Baal \q and led {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel astray.

L.13: And among the prophets of Samaria I saw something offensive: \q they prophesied by Baal \q and led {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel astray.

R.13: I saw something disgusting among the prophets of Samaria: \q they spoke messages in the name of Baal \q and led {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel the wrong way.

decisions.choice: Samaria: the capital of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Samaria was the royal city of Israel, the northern kingdom, which fell to Assyria in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:5-18). Under King Ahab its prophets served Baal (1 Kings 18:19).

decisions.choice: something offensive: an unseemly, senseless thing
decisions.reason: The word means something tasteless or improper (Job 1:22; 24:12). It is milder than the word for Jerusalem's prophets in verse 14: what Samaria's prophets did was bad, Jerusalem's is worse.

decisions.choice: prophesied by Baal: speaking in Baal's name, as his prophets
decisions.reason: The prophets claimed that their messages came from Baal (2:8). Jeremiah reminds Judah that this is what brought the northern kingdom to ruin.

records.source: וּבִנְבִאֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם רָאִ֣יתִי שַׁעֲרוּרָ֗ה נָא֞וֹף וְהָלֹ֤ךְ בַּשֶּׁ֨קֶר֙ וְחִזְּקוּ֙ יְדֵ֣י מְרֵעִ֔ים לְבִ֨לְתִּי־שָׁ֔בוּ אִ֖ישׁ מֵרָֽעָת֑וֹ הָֽיוּ־לִ֤י כֻלָּם֙ כִּסְדֹ֔ם וְיֹשְׁבֶ֖יהָ כַּעֲמֹרָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And among [the] prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: committing adultery and walking in falsehood, and they strengthen [the] hands of evildoers, so that not they turn back, each from his evil; they have become to me all of them like Sodom, and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.
pieces: But among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen something horrible: \q they commit adultery and live by lies. \q They strengthen the hands of those who do evil, so that no one turns away from wickedness. \q To {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they have all become like Sodom, \q and the people of the city like Gomorrah.

L.14: But among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: \q committing adultery and walking in falsehood; \q and they strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns back from {{gender:their|his}} evil. \q All of them have become to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} like Sodom, \q and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.

R.14: But among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen something horrible: \q they are unfaithful in marriage, and they live by lies. \q They encourage people who do evil, so that no one stops doing wrong. \q To {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they are all like the people of Sodom, \q and the people of Jerusalem are like Gomorrah.

decisions.choice: a horrible thing: something that makes one shudder
decisions.reason: The word is used for the most shocking wrongs (5:30; 18:13; Hosea 6:10). Jerusalem's prophets are worse than Samaria's (verse 13).

decisions.choice: strengthen the hands of evildoers: encourage them to keep on
decisions.reason: To strengthen someone's hands is to give them courage to act (Judges 9:24; Ezra 6:22). By promising peace (verse 17), the prophets make the wicked feel safe.

decisions.choice: like Sodom and Gomorrah: cities known for their evil and their destruction
decisions.reason: Sodom and Gomorrah were destroyed for their wickedness (Genesis 18:20; 19:24-25), and the prophets compare Jerusalem to them (Isaiah 1:10; Ezekiel 16:46-50). "Its inhabitants" are the people of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: encourage
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means (m2).

decisions.choice: the people of the city (Balanced); the people of Jerusalem (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Its inhabitants" refers to Jerusalem; Balanced and Readable make that clear.

records.source: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ עַל־הַנְּבִאִ֔ים הִנְנִ֨י מַאֲכִ֤יל אוֹתָם֙ לַֽעֲנָ֔ה וְהִשְׁקִתִ֖ים מֵי־רֹ֑אשׁ כִּ֗י מֵאֵת֙ נְבִיאֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם יָצְאָ֥ה חֲנֻפָּ֖ה לְכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃פ
records.gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh of hosts concerning the prophets: look, I [am] feeding them wormwood and I will make them drink water of poison, for from the prophets of Jerusalem has gone out godlessness to all the land.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this about the prophets: \q I am going to feed them bitter wormwood \q and give them poisoned water to drink, \q because from the prophets of Jerusalem \q godlessness has spread through the whole land.

L.15: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts concerning the prophets: \q Look, I am feeding them wormwood \q and I will make them drink poisoned water; \q for from the prophets of Jerusalem \q godlessness has gone out into all the land.

R.15: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says about the prophets: \q I am going to give them bitter plants to eat \q and poisoned water to drink. \q The prophets of Jerusalem \q have spread godlessness through the whole land.

decisions.choice: wormwood and poisoned water: the same words as 9:14
decisions.reason: God said this of the whole people in 9:14; now he says it of the prophets. Wormwood is a bitter plant; the second word names a poisonous plant, and water mixed with it is bitter and deadly. The picture is of a judgment as bitter as their sin (8:14).

decisions.choice: godlessness: the corruption of verse 11
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb of verse 11, "polluted". The corruption that began with the prophets has spread through the land.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this title, as in Isaiah. Readable says "bitter plants" for wormwood, as in 9:14.

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אַֽל־תִּשְׁמְע֞וּ עַל־דִּבְרֵ֤י הַנְּבִאִים֙ הַנִּבְּאִ֣ים לָכֶ֔ם מַהְבִּלִ֥ים הֵ֖מָּה אֶתְכֶ֑ם חֲז֤וֹן לִבָּם֙ יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ לֹ֖א מִפִּ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: do not listen to [the] words of the prophets prophesying to you; they [are] making you vain; a vision of their heart they speak, not from [the] mouth of Yahweh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Do not listen to what the prophets are prophesying to you; \q they are filling you with empty hopes. \q They speak visions that come from their own minds, \q and not from the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you; \q they are filling you with vanity; \q a vision of their own heart they speak, \q not from the mouth of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Do not listen to what the prophets are telling you. \q They are giving you false hopes. \q The visions they tell you come from their own minds, \q not from what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said.

decisions.choice: filling you with vanity: leading you into emptiness
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a breath or vapor, something empty and worthless. Those who follow emptiness become empty (2:5). The prophets give the people hopes that have nothing in them.

decisions.choice: a vision of their own heart: something they made up
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is where a person thinks and plans. The prophets' visions come out of their own thoughts and wishes (14:14), not from God.

decisions.choice: from the mouth of the LORD: spoken by God himself
decisions.reason: A true prophet speaks what God puts in his mouth (1:9; 15:19; Deuteronomy 18:18).

decisions.choice: minds
decisions.reason: "Heart" here means the mind and its thoughts, so Balanced and Readable say "minds".

records.source: אֹמְרִ֤ים אָמוֹר֙ לִֽמְנַאֲצַ֔י דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שָׁל֖וֹם יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם וְ֠כֹל הֹלֵ֞ךְ בִּשְׁרִר֤וּת לִבּוֹ֙ אָֽמְר֔וּ לֹֽא־תָב֥וֹא עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם רָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: Saying continually to those despising me: Yahweh has spoken, peace will be to you; and [to] everyone walking in [the] stubbornness of his heart they say: not will come upon you disaster.
pieces: They keep telling those who despise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says you will have peace." \q And to all who follow the stubbornness of their own hearts they say, "No disaster will come on you."

L.17: They keep saying to those who despise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: Peace will be yours"; \q and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of {{gender:their|his}} heart they say, "Disaster will not come upon you."

R.17: They keep telling people who despise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says you will have peace." \q They tell everyone who stubbornly follows their own heart, "Nothing bad will happen to you."

decisions.choice: to those who despise me, "The LORD has spoken" (the Hebrew text)
alternatives: to those who despise the word of the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels read "to those who despise me: the LORD has spoken". The same consonants can be read "to those who despise the word of the LORD", and the Septuagint seems to read it that way. The Hebrew reading is kept; either way the prophets comfort people who reject God. This claim about the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: Peace will be yours: the false prophets' message
decisions.reason: This is what the prophets kept saying while disaster drew near (6:14; 8:11; 14:13). Peace here is safety and well-being, the opposite of the "disaster" they deny.

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of their heart: doing what one wants and refusing God
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's word for the people's stiff refusal to listen (3:17; 7:24; 9:13; Deuteronomy 29:18).

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of their heart (Literal); the stubbornness of their own hearts (Balanced); stubbornly follows their own heart (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for this phrase. Balanced does not add "evil" here because the Hebrew does not have it.

records.source: כִּ֣י מִ֤י עָמַד֙ בְּס֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה וְיֵ֖רֶא וְיִשְׁמַ֣ע אֶת־דְּבָר֑וֹ מִֽי־הִקְשִׁ֥יב דְּבָר֖וֹ וַיִּשְׁמָֽע׃ס
records.gloss: For who has stood in [the] council of Yahweh and seen and heard his word? Who has paid attention to his word and listened?
pieces: For who has stood in the council of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} \q to see and to hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word? \q Who has listened closely to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word and heard it?

L.18: For who has stood in the council of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and seen and heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word? \q Who has paid attention to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word and listened?

R.18: Who has stood in the council of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} plans, to see and hear {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} message? \q Who has paid attention and listened to what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says?

decisions.choice: the council of the LORD: the gathering around God's throne where his plans are made known
decisions.reason: The word means a circle of people who talk together in confidence. The Bible pictures God surrounded by heavenly beings who hear his decisions (1 Kings 22:19-22; Job 15:8; Psalm 89:8). A true prophet is one who has been let into that council and hears God's purposes from God himself (verse 22; Amos 3:7).

decisions.choice: who has stood ...?: a question that expects the answer "none of them"
decisions.reason: The question is aimed at the prophets of verses 16-17. Verse 22 gives the answer: if they had stood in God's council, they would have spoken his words.

decisions.choice: his word (the form read aloud)
decisions.reason: In the second line the written consonants give "my word", and the scribes marked "his word" to be read aloud, matching the first line. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: where he makes his plans
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the council is (m1).

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה׀סַעֲרַ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה חֵמָה֙ יָֽצְאָ֔ה וְסַ֖עַר מִתְחוֹלֵ֑ל עַ֛ל רֹ֥אשׁ רְשָׁעִ֖ים יָחֽוּל׃
records.gloss: Look, [the] storm of Yahweh, wrath has gone out, and a storm whirling; on [the] head of [the] wicked it will whirl.
pieces: Look, the storm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Fury has burst out, \q a whirlwind spinning around; \q it will crash down on the heads of the wicked.

L.19: Look, the storm of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Wrath has gone out, \q a whirling tempest; \q on the head of the wicked it will whirl down.

R.19: Look! The anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is like a storm. \q It has broken out like a whirlwind, \q and it will strike the heads of wicked people.

decisions.choice: verses 19-20 come back in 30:23-24
decisions.reason: The same two verses are repeated almost word for word in 30:23-24, where they close a promise of restoration. Here they answer the false promise of "no disaster" in verse 17.

decisions.choice: the storm of the LORD: his anger pictured as a violent storm
decisions.reason: Wind and storm picture God's judgment coming suddenly and with force (4:11-13; 25:32; Isaiah 29:6).

decisions.choice: The anger of the LORD is like a storm
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means and joins "storm" and "wrath" in one sentence.

records.source: לֹ֤א יָשׁוּב֙ אַף־יְהוָ֔ה עַד־עֲשֹׂת֥וֹ וְעַד־הֲקִימ֖וֹ מְזִמּ֣וֹת לִבּ֑וֹ בְּאַֽחֲרִית֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים תִּתְבּ֥וֹנְנוּ בָ֖הּ בִּינָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not will turn back [the] anger of Yahweh until he has done and until he has carried out [the] purposes of his heart; in [the] latter part of the days you will understand it [with] understanding.
pieces: The anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not turn away \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has fully carried out what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has purposed in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart. \q In the days ahead \q you will understand it fully.

L.20: The anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not turn back \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done and until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has carried out the purposes of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heart. \q In the latter days \q you will understand it clearly.

R.20: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will not stop being angry \q until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned. \q Later on, \q you will understand this clearly.

decisions.choice: the latter days: the time to come, after the judgment
decisions.reason: The phrase means the later part of time, the future as seen from now. In Jeremiah it often points to the time after judgment (30:24; 48:47; 49:39). Then the people will see that the prophet spoke the truth.

decisions.choice: you will understand it clearly: the same root twice for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun come from the same root, a Hebrew way of saying "fully". "You" is plural: the people.

decisions.choice: fully carried out what he has purposed
decisions.reason: Balanced joins the two verbs "done ... carried out" into one phrase.

records.source: לֹא־שָׁלַ֥חְתִּי אֶת־הַנְּבִאִ֖ים וְהֵ֣ם רָ֑צוּ לֹא־דִבַּ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְהֵ֥ם נִבָּֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: Not I sent the prophets, and they ran; not I spoke to them, and they prophesied.
pieces: I did not send these prophets, but they ran anyway. \q I did not speak to them, but they prophesied all the same.

L.21: I did not send the prophets, yet they ran; \q I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.

R.21: I did not send these prophets, but they rushed out anyway. \q I did not speak to them, but they still gave messages.

decisions.choice: they ran: like messengers hurrying with news
decisions.reason: A runner carried a message from a king or commander (2 Samuel 18:19-23). These prophets ran with a message nobody gave them (14:14).

decisions.choice: the prophets: those just described
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "the prophets", meaning the ones God has been speaking about since verse 9.

decisions.choice: these prophets
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "these" to make clear which prophets are meant.

records.source: וְאִֽם־עָמְד֖וּ בְּסוֹדִ֑י וְיַשְׁמִ֤עוּ דְבָרַי֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וִֽישִׁבוּם֙ מִדַּרְכָּ֣ם הָרָ֔ע וּמֵרֹ֖עַ מַֽעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And if they had stood in my council, and they would have made hear my words my people and turned them back from their way the evil and from [the] evil of their deeds.
pieces: But if they had stood in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} council, \q they would have announced {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people \q and turned them from their evil path \q and from their wicked deeds.

L.22: But if they had stood in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} council, \q then they would have made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, \q and they would have turned them back from their evil way \q and from the evil of their deeds.

R.22: If they had stood in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} council, \q they would have told {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messages. \q They would have turned them away from their evil ways \q and the evil things they do.

decisions.choice: turned them back from their evil way: the mark of a true prophet
decisions.reason: A prophet sent by God calls the people to turn from evil (18:11; 25:5; 26:3; 35:15). The false prophets did the opposite: they made the wicked feel safe (verses 14, 17).

decisions.choice: if they had stood ... they would have: a condition that did not happen
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what would have followed if the prophets had heard God. They did not, and so the people were not warned.

records.gloss: A God from near [am] I, declares Yahweh, and not a God from far?
pieces: Am I a God who is only near, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and not a God who is far away?

L.23: Am I a God from near at hand, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and not a God from far away?

R.23: Am I only a God who is close by, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? \q Am I not also a God who is far away?

decisions.choice: near and far: God is not a small god at hand that people can manage
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "No". The prophets speak as if God were close by and easy to please, a god who would never judge his people. But he is the God who is high above and sees everything from afar (Psalm 139:2; Isaiah 57:15), so nothing is hidden from him (verse 24).

decisions.choice: a question (the Hebrew text)
alternatives: I am a God near at hand and not a God far off
decisions.reason: The Hebrew marks the sentence as a question. The Septuagint seems to read it as a statement, "I am a God who is near, and not a God far off", stressing that God is near and sees. The Hebrew is kept. This claim about the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: only near (Balanced); only ... close by, also ... far away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "only" and "also" to make clear what the question means (m1).

L.24: Or can anyone hide in hiding places so that I do not see {{gender:them|him}}? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Do I not fill the heavens and the earth? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.24: Can anyone hide in a secret place where I cannot see {{gender:them|him}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q I fill all of heaven and earth, do I not? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: I fill the heavens and the earth: God is present everywhere
decisions.reason: No place is outside God's reach, so no prophet can hide his lies from him (Psalm 139:7-12; Amos 9:2-3; 1 Kings 8:27).

decisions.choice: anyone: any person, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word often means "a man", but here it means "anyone".

decisions.choice: I fill all of heaven and earth, do I not?
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the question but puts the statement first so the answer is plain.

records.source: שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֵ֤ת אֲשֶׁר־אָֽמְרוּ֙ הַנְּבִאִ֔ים הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים בִּשְׁמִ֛י שֶׁ֖קֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר חָלַ֖מְתִּי חָלָֽמְתִּי׃

pieces: I have heard what the prophets say who prophesy lies in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. They say, "I had a dream! I had a dream!"

L.25: I have heard what the prophets have said who prophesy falsehood in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, saying, "I have dreamed, I have dreamed!"

R.25: I have heard the prophets who tell lies and say they speak for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. They say, "I had a dream! I had a dream!"

decisions.choice: I have dreamed: a claim to have received a message from God in a dream
decisions.reason: God could speak through dreams (Numbers 12:6; Genesis 28:12-15), but a dream did not prove that a prophet was sent by him (Deuteronomy 13:2-6). The cry is repeated to sound urgent and convincing.

decisions.choice: in my name: claiming to speak for God
decisions.reason: To prophesy in God's name is to say that the message comes from him (14:14-15; 27:15; 29:9).

decisions.choice: say they speak for me
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in my name" means (m2).

L.26: How long? Is it in the heart of the prophets who prophesy falsehood, the prophets of the deceit of their own heart,

R.26: How long will these prophets go on telling lies? They prophesy what their own deceitful minds make up.

decisions.choice: How long ... in the heart of the prophets: a broken-off question
alternatives: Is there anything in the hearts of the prophets?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and hard: "Until when? Is there in the heart of the prophets ...?" It may mean "How long will this be in their hearts?" or "Is there anything at all in their hearts?" The sentence runs on into verse 27, which says what they plan. Either way God asks how long their lying will go on.

decisions.choice: the deceit of their own heart: lies they invent
decisions.reason: As in verse 16 and 14:14, the heart is where they think up what they say.

decisions.choice: How long will these prophets go on telling lies? (two sentences)
decisions.reason: Readable makes two short sentences of the run-on question and starts a new sentence in verse 27.

pieces: who plan to make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people forget {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name with the dreams they tell one another, just as their ancestors forgot {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name because of Baal?

L.27: who plan to make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people forget {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name by their dreams that they recount, each to {{gender:their|his}} neighbor, just as their fathers forgot {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name through Baal?

R.27: With the dreams they tell one another, they plan to make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people forget {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, just as their ancestors forgot {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name by worshiping Baal.

decisions.choice: forget my name: forget God himself and who he is
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God as he has made himself known. To forget it is to stop worshiping and obeying him (2:32; Psalm 44:21).

decisions.choice: as their fathers forgot my name through Baal: the same sin as before
decisions.reason: In the days of the judges and of Ahab, Israel turned to Baal and forgot the LORD (Judges 3:7; 1 Kings 18:21; Hosea 2:15). The dream prophets lead the people the same way, even when they speak in the LORD's name.

decisions.choice: by worshiping Baal
decisions.reason: Readable says how Baal made them forget: they worshiped him.

records.gloss: The prophet who [is] with him a dream, let him recount a dream, and [he] who my word [is] with him, let him speak my word [in] faithfulness. What [is] to the straw with the grain? declares Yahweh.
pieces: Let the prophet who has a dream tell it as a dream, but let the one who has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word faithfully. What does straw have in common with grain? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.28: The prophet who has a dream, let him recount a dream; and the one who has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, let him speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word faithfully. What [has] the straw [to do] with the grain? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.28: If a prophet has had a dream, let him say it is only a dream. But if someone has {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} message, let that person speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} message faithfully. Straw is nothing like grain! says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: let him recount a dream: let him call it a dream and nothing more
decisions.reason: God does not forbid telling dreams. He sets a dream beside his word: let a dream be told as a dream, and not passed off as the word of the LORD.

decisions.choice: faithfully: in truth, as it was given
decisions.reason: The word means truth and faithfulness. The prophet who has God's word must pass it on as he received it, adding nothing and leaving nothing out (26:2).

decisions.choice: straw and grain: the worthless set beside the real thing
decisions.reason: When grain was threshed, the straw and chaff were separated from the kernels (Psalm 1:4). The prophets' dreams are straw; God's word is the grain that feeds.

decisions.choice: Straw is nothing like grain!
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

records.gloss: [Is] not thus my word like fire, declares Yahweh, and like a hammer [that] shatters rock?
pieces: Is not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word like fire, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like a hammer that smashes rock to pieces?

L.29: Is not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word like this, like fire, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and like a hammer that shatters rock?

R.29: My word is like fire, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is like a hammer that smashes rocks to pieces.

decisions.choice: my word like fire: God's word burns and cannot be held back
decisions.reason: God told Jeremiah that his words in the prophet's mouth would be fire that burns up the people like wood (5:14), and Jeremiah felt it as a fire shut up in his bones (20:9). Unlike the prophets' dreams, it does what it says.

decisions.choice: a hammer that shatters rock: nothing can stand against it
decisions.reason: The verb means to break into pieces. God's word breaks down the hardest resistance.

decisions.choice: My word is like fire (a statement)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question, which expects the answer "yes", into a statement.

records.source: לָכֵ֛ן הִנְנִ֥י עַל־הַנְּבִאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה מְגַנְּבֵ֣י דְבָרַ֔י אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֵ֥ת רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore look, I [am] against the prophets, declares Yahweh, stealing my words each from his neighbor.
pieces: So I am against the prophets, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who steal {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words from one another.

L.30: Therefore look, I [am] against the prophets, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who steal {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, each from {{gender:their|his}} neighbor.

R.30: So I am against these prophets, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They steal messages from each other and say they are {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.

decisions.choice: I am against: God sets himself as their enemy
decisions.reason: The phrase "look, I am against ..." announces that God will act against someone (21:13; 50:31; Ezekiel 13:8).

decisions.choice: steal my words: pass off borrowed words as God's
decisions.reason: Having no word of their own from God, they take phrases from one another, or from true prophets, and present them as a message from the LORD.

decisions.choice: and say they are mine
decisions.reason: Readable says what "steal my words" means (m2).

records.source: הִנְנִ֥י עַל־הַנְּבִיאִ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה הַלֹּקְחִ֣ים לְשׁוֹנָ֔ם וַֽיִּנְאֲמ֖וּ נְאֻֽם׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] against the prophets, declares Yahweh, taking their tongue and declaring, [it is] a declaration.
pieces: I am against the prophets, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who speak with their own tongues and then announce, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} declares."

L.31: Look, I [am] against the prophets, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who take their own tongues and declare, "Declares [{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}]."

R.31: I am against these prophets, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They make up their own messages and then say, "This is a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: declare, "Declares": a play on the prophets' formula
decisions.reason: The noun "declaration" is the word in the formula "declares the LORD", which closes many of God's sayings in this chapter. The prophets use only their own tongues and then add the formula, borrowing God's authority for their own words.

decisions.choice: Declares [the LORD] (Literal); The LORD declares (Balanced); This is a message from the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the word of the formula alone. English supplies "the LORD" so that the reader can recognize the formula.

records.source: הִ֠נְנִי עַֽל־נִבְּאֵ֞י חֲלֹמ֥וֹת שֶׁ֨קֶר֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וַֽיְסַפְּרוּם֙ וַיַּתְע֣וּ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י בְּשִׁקְרֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְפַחֲזוּתָ֑ם וְאָנֹכִ֨י לֹֽא־שְׁלַחְתִּ֜ים וְלֹ֣א צִוִּיתִ֗ים וְהוֹעֵ֛יל לֹֽא־יוֹעִ֥ילוּ לָֽעָם־הַזֶּ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Look, I [am] against those prophesying dreams of falsehood, declares Yahweh, and they recount them and lead astray my people by their falsehoods and by their recklessness, and I not sent them and not commanded them, and benefit not they will benefit this people, declares Yahweh.
pieces: I am against those who prophesy false dreams, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They tell them and lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people astray with their lies and their reckless boasting, though I did not send them or give them any command. They do this people no good at all, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.32: Look, I [am] against those who prophesy false dreams, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and recount them and lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people astray by their falsehoods and by their recklessness, though I did not send them and did not command them; and they will not benefit this people at all, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.32: I am against the prophets who tell false dreams, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They tell these dreams and lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people the wrong way with their lies and their wild boasting. But I did not send them or give them orders. They do not help these people at all, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: recklessness: wild, boastful talk
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root used of people who are reckless and undisciplined (Judges 9:4), and of prophets who are "reckless" (Zephaniah 3:4). Here it is the prophets' careless, swaggering talk.

decisions.choice: not benefit at all: the doubled verb for emphasis
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated, a Hebrew way of saying "not in the least". The same verb is used for idols that cannot help (2:8, 11; 16:19).

decisions.choice: reckless boasting (Balanced); wild boasting (Readable)
decisions.reason: The phrase brings out both sides of the word (m1).

records.gloss: And when asks you this people or the prophet or a priest, saying: what [is the] burden of Yahweh? then you will say to them: what burden? and I will cast you off, declares Yahweh.
pieces: When this people, or a prophet or a priest, asks you, "What is {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden?" you are to say to them, "What burden? I will throw you off, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.33: And when this people or the prophet or a priest asks you, saying, "What [is] the burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}?" then you will say to them, "What burden? I will cast you off, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.33: When these people, or a prophet or a priest, ask you, "What is {{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden? What message does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} have for us?" tell them, "What burden? I will throw you away, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: burden: both a heavy load and a message from God
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to lift, to carry". It means a load that is carried, and it is also the usual title for a prophet's message (Isaiah 13:1; 15:1; Nahum 1:1), something "lifted up" by the voice, often a heavy word of judgment. Verses 33-40 play on both senses: the people ask mockingly for the LORD's latest "burden", and God answers that they themselves are a load he will throw off.

decisions.choice: "What burden?" (the Hebrew text)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "What burden?" The same consonants, divided differently, read "You are the burden", and the Septuagint and the Latin Vulgate have that reading: "You are the burden, and I will cast you off." The Hebrew is kept; both readings say that the people, not God's word, are the weight God will throw down. This claim about the ancient versions is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: you: Jeremiah
decisions.reason: God speaks to the prophet, telling him how to answer those who ask for a "burden".

decisions.choice: cast off: let fall, abandon
decisions.reason: The verb means to let something fall or to leave it lying, as a load is thrown down (7:29; 12:7). It fits the picture of the burden.

decisions.choice: burden at every level; Readable adds "What message does he have for us?"
decisions.reason: Only a word that means both a load and a message keeps the play of verses 33-40, and "burden" is kept in every verse so that the play can be followed. Readable adds a question that says what the people mean by it.

decisions.reason: The phrase has become a mocking catchword, or a false claim to a message from God. Anyone who uses it, even a prophet or priest, will be punished (verses 36, 38).

decisions.reason: God will "attend to" the speaker, that is, deal with him for what he has done.

decisions.choice: anyone else
decisions.reason: "The people" here means any of the people, so Balanced and Readable say "anyone else".

records.source: כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֛וּ אִ֥ישׁ עַל־רֵעֵ֖הוּ וְאִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֑יו מֶה־עָנָ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה וּמַה־דִּבֶּ֖ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus you will say, each to his neighbor and each to his brother: what has answered Yahweh? and what has spoken Yahweh?
pieces: This is what each of you is to say to your friends and relatives: "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered?" or "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said?"

L.35: Thus you will say, each to {{gender:their|his}} neighbor and each to {{gender:their|his}} {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}: "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered?" and "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken?"

R.35: Instead, when you talk with your friends and family, ask, "What answer has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} given?" or "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said?"

decisions.choice: What has the LORD answered? What has the LORD spoken?: plain words to use instead
decisions.reason: The people are to ask simply what God has said, without the loaded word "burden".

decisions.choice: neighbor ... brother: one another, friend and relative
decisions.reason: The pair means the people around a person, whether neighbors or family.

decisions.choice: Instead
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link with verse 34 plain.

records.source: וּמַשָּׂ֥א יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א תִזְכְּרוּ־ע֑וֹד כִּ֣י הַמַּשָּׂ֗א יִֽהְיֶה֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ דְּבָר֔וֹ וַהֲפַכְתֶּ֗ם אֶת־דִּבְרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חַיִּ֔ים יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] burden of Yahweh not you will mention again, for the burden will be to each man his word, and you have perverted [the] words of [the] God living, Yahweh of hosts, our God.
pieces: But you must never again speak of "{{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden," because each person's own word will become their burden, and you twist the words of the living God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, our God.

L.36: But "the burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}" you shall not mention again, for the burden will be to each one {{gender:their|his}} own word; and you have twisted the words of the living God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, our God.

R.36: But you must stop saying "{{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden." Each person's own words will become a heavy burden for them. You have twisted the words of the living God, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, our God.

decisions.choice: the burden will be to each one their own word: their own words will weigh on them
alternatives: each one's own word is his oracle
decisions.reason: The words can be read in two ways: each person's own word becomes his "burden", the load that crushes him; or each one calls his own word a "burden", passing off his own ideas as a message from God. The first fits the play of verse 33. The rendering keeps the Hebrew's openness at Literal and Balanced; Readable follows the first reading.

decisions.choice: the living God: the God who acts, unlike lifeless idols
decisions.reason: God is called "the living God" in contrast with idols (10:10). The prophets twist the words of the one God who is truly alive.

decisions.choice: Each person's own words will become a heavy burden for them
decisions.reason: Readable follows the first reading in m1.

records.source: כֹּ֥ה תֹאמַ֖ר אֶל־הַנָּבִ֑יא מֶה־עָנָ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה וּמַה־דִּבֶּ֖ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus you will say to the prophet: what has answered you Yahweh? and what has spoken Yahweh?
pieces: This is how you are to speak to a prophet: "What answer has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} given you?" or "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said?"

L.37: Thus you will say to the prophet, "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered you?" and "What has {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoken?"

R.37: When you speak to a prophet, ask, "What answer did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} give you?" or "What did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} say?"

decisions.choice: you will say ... answered you: each person speaking to a prophet
decisions.reason: "You will say" is singular here: each person is to put the question this way. The ending on "answered you" is unusual in form, but it plainly refers to the prophet being asked.

decisions.choice: the prophet: any prophet
decisions.reason: The question is for any prophet, true or false. A true one can answer it.

records.source: וְאִם־מַשָּׂ֣א יְהוָה֮ תֹּאמֵרוּ֒ לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה יַ֧עַן אֲמָרְכֶ֛ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה מַשָּׂ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וָאֶשְׁלַ֤ח אֲלֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א תֹאמְר֖וּ מַשָּׂ֥א יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And if [the] burden of Yahweh you say, therefore thus says Yahweh: because you have said this word, [the] burden of Yahweh, and I sent to you, saying, not you shall say, [the] burden of Yahweh,
pieces: But if you do say, "{{divine_name:The LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden," then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Because you have used these words, "{{divine_name:The LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden," even though I sent word to you and said, "Do not say, '{{divine_name:The LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden,'"

L.38: But if you say, "The burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Because you have said this word, "The burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," though I sent to you, saying, "You shall not say, 'The burden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},'"

R.38: But suppose you keep saying "{{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden." Then this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I sent you a message telling you not to say "{{divine_name:the LORD's|Yahweh's}} burden." But you have said it anyway.

decisions.choice: because: the reason for the judgment in verses 39-40
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 39: because they keep using the word after God forbade it, he will throw them off.

decisions.choice: I sent to you: God's command came through his prophet
decisions.reason: God sent the message of verses 34-36 through Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: I sent you a message ... But you have said it anyway. (new sentences)
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the reason in short sentences and begins the judgment with a new sentence in verse 39.

records.source: לָכֵ֣ן הִנְנִ֔י וְנָשִׁ֥יתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם נָשֹׁ֑א וְנָטַשְׁתִּ֣י אֶתְכֶ֗ם וְאֶת־הָעִיר֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧תִּי לָכֶ֛ם וְלַאֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם מֵעַ֥ל פָּנָֽי׃
records.gloss: therefore look, I will forget you, forgetting, and I will cast off you and the city that I gave to you and to your fathers from before my face,
pieces: therefore I will forget you completely and throw you away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence, you and the city I gave to you and your ancestors,

L.39: therefore look, I will surely forget you, and I will cast you away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence, you and the city that I gave to you and to your fathers,

R.39: So I will forget all about you. I will throw you out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight, you and the city I gave to you and your ancestors.

decisions.choice: I will surely forget you (the Hebrew text)
alternatives: I will surely lift you up
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "I will forget you". A few Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient versions have a verb that differs by one letter, "I will lift you up", the root of "burden": God would pick the people up like a load and throw it away. The Hebrew is kept. This claim about the manuscripts and versions is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: cast you away: the verb of verse 33
decisions.reason: God does to them what he warned in verse 33: he throws them down like a load.

decisions.choice: the city I gave to you and to your fathers: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was God's gift with the land (7:7, 14). Being thrown away from his presence means exile from the city and the temple (7:15).

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֥י עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם חֶרְפַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם וּכְלִמּ֣וּת עוֹלָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר לֹ֥א תִשָּׁכֵֽחַ׃ס
records.gloss: and I will put on you a reproach of perpetuity and a shame of perpetuity which not will be forgotten.
pieces: and I will make you a disgrace for all time, an everlasting shame that will never be forgotten.

L.40: and I will put on you everlasting reproach and everlasting shame, which will not be forgotten.

R.40: I will bring disgrace on you that will last forever. Your shame will never be forgotten.

decisions.choice: everlasting shame that will not be forgotten: the same words as 20:11
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses these words in 20:11 of his persecutors. Here they close the chapter: God will "forget" the people (verse 39), but their shame will not be forgotten.

decisions.choice: everlasting: lasting into the far future
decisions.reason: The word means a very long time, without a set end. It is the shame of the exile, remembered long after.

decisions.choice: disgrace, shame
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "disgrace" for the first word, which means scorn heaped on someone.
